planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, siting it where its unusually low profile will not be lost behind taller neighbors.

directions: Springbrook is among the most dwarf of the named green-and-gold selections, forming a dense low mat of scalloped, semi-evergreen foliage that stays just a few inches off the ground, noticeably flatter than Allen Bush or the species itself. Five-petaled, bright yellow, star-shaped flowers rise just above the leaves from mid-spring into summer, drawing small native bees to a plant most gardeners use as a tight edging or small-scale woodland groundcover rather than a tall filler. It spreads gradually by short stolons to knit together a weed-suppressing carpet without becoming aggressive, so it fits well along shaded path edges, in rock gardens, or tucked among stepping stones. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, dividing congested patches every few years in spring to maintain density.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center
